Stickyickistan is an island on the planet of [[Mythmos]], shrouded in magic and home to one of the largest economies in the realms. Its wealth is built primarily on the cultivation and export of [[Arcannabis]], along with trade in [[Arcanite]] and other resources. The island’s size and distance from other landmasses are difficult to measure. Even the most sophisticated magic and technology fails beyond a certain distance from its shores.

The waters around Stickyickistan form a region much like a magical Bermuda Triangle. Pilots and sailors report violent weather, distorted horizons, impossible currents, and terrifying creatures from above and below. Vast deposits of [[Arcanite]] beneath [[Mount Zooka]] have warped time, space, and the Weave around the island, producing these phenomena and making accurate maps difficult to create. Stickyickistan can be seen from [[Lumytholarispace]] and appears on maps of Mythmos, but it always looks smaller than it seems when approached.

![[Stickyickistan.jpg]]

# Modern Stickyickistan

Stickyickistan is a city-state built around an active volcano. Approximately 27 million people live across its dense network of terraced districts. The Capitol stands on [[Nevercough Island]], a smaller landmass sheltered within an inlet on the main island. The climate is generally tropical, with hot, humid weather dominating the city. Farther inland, however, desertification has created increasingly arid regions, a legacy of [[Human Colonialism]] and industrialization.

Upscale residences climb from the volcano’s base into lush jungle, where they overlook the ocean. The immense canopy of trees, some resembling gigantic redwoods, provides a natural shield against volcanic eruptions. Below these elevated neighborhoods, settlements cling to the mountainside in a haze of ash, smoke, brimstone, and sulfur. Above them, an industrial district follows the crater’s rim and extends into the volcano itself.

The centerpiece of the city is [[Mount Zooka]], an [[Arcanite]] Cone. These volcanoes form above rich Arcanite deposits and rise as vast mounds of black volcanic rock. Dark, sluggish lava flows around the mountain’s base, while a crater filled with bubbling magma crowns its summit. Eruptions scatter volcanic stones, molten rock, and occasional chunks of Arcanite across the surrounding slopes. Afterward, workers harvest the valuable ores and minerals from the crater.

Arcanite is a raw magical element normally found deep underground. Once extracted and purified, it can grant magical properties to weapons and armor. The government, formally the [[Nevercough Tribunal]], maintains mines and outposts in and around the crater so workers have shelter during their shifts.

The island’s soil is rich in nutrients and infused with traces of Arcanite. As a result, its flora and fauna grow with extraordinary fertility and magical potency. This energy affects forest creatures, vegetation, and occasionally city dwellers. [[Dabnar Nevercough]], the Chief Magistrate, serves as both head of state and Supreme Judge. [[Arcannabis]] remains the city-state’s primary export, while Arcanite and other natural resources provide additional wealth.

Since the arrival of human colonists, alcohol has been outlawed because the government considers it a threat to the Arcannabis market. [[Zooka Malt]], a beverage made from Arcannabis buds, has become the principal alternative to traditional ale, with countless infused varieties sold throughout the city. [[Nevercough Island]] is home to the city-state’s most exclusive shops, courthouses, museums, galleries, libraries, and other cultural institutions.

South of Nevercough Island and north of the volcano lies [[Lower South Booftown]], commonly called [[Booftown]]. This middle-class district is known for family-owned shops and public parks. A slow-moving river of thick, dark lava separates it from [[Upper South Booftown]], also called [[The Ashtray]]. The Ashtray houses much of the city’s criminal underworld and is home to several notorious gangs. The MOB, or [[Mandem on Booftown]], and the CCC, or [[Cough City Crew]], compete for territory and control of illicit substances, weapons, arcane artifacts, and money.

Upper South Booftown is home primarily to the native Halfling population and other minority communities. The MOB remains exclusively Halfling, while the CCC includes Halflings, Humans, and members of other peoples.

To the east of the volcano lies [[Bobo Bush Estates]], a district of mansions and villas belonging to Stickyickistan’s wealthiest and most influential residents. North of Nevercough Island, [[North Booftown]] serves as the agricultural heartland. It is also home to [[House Northbourne]], a Human criminal enterprise specializing in extortion, gambling, and the illicit distribution of bootleg alcohol. The group uses a bookmaking business as a front for money laundering and owns the North Booftown Downs racetrack. The Norfies have been accused of fixing races and operating illegal gambling networks.

On the western side of the city, [[Bongstad]] is a Dwarven settlement carved into the base of Mount Zooka. Its engineers developed a magical geothermal power system that supplies much of the region’s [[Magitech]] grid. Bongstad is also known for producing some of the finest forges on the island.

Beyond the city lies [[The Outback]], a vast expanse of arcane forests, swamps, bogs, mountains, jungles, rainforests, beaches, badlands, and desert. Creatures from across the Material Plane and beyond inhabit the region. The pure magic released by Mount Zooka has made Stickyickistan a hotspot in the multiverse.

# Past Stickyickistan

Stickyickistan did not always have its current tropical climate. In earlier ages, the island maintained a more balanced pattern of hot and cold regions, as well as arid and humid zones. The northern part once held an ice cap, while the south resembled a Mediterranean climate more than a Caribbean one. Industrialization caused severe climate change. Rising temperatures melted the ice cap and turned some old-growth forests into desert. Recent conservation efforts have slowed the damage, but much of the original landscape has been lost.

## [[Human Colonialism]]

Long ago, the island’s only humanoid inhabitants were peaceful Halfling communities. They followed a polytheistic faith devoted to [[The Three Sisters]], lived in close relationship with the land, and respected the creatures that shared it. The island flourished, its soil was fertile, and its forests teemed with life.

That balance was disrupted when ambitious Human settlers arrived. Seeking control of the island’s resources, they treated the Halflings as obstacles and launched a violent invasion. The settlers established [[Nevercough City]] on what they called [[Nevercough Island]], forming the nation that would eventually become Stickyickistan.

The Halflings resisted, but they were outnumbered and outmatched. Their leaders eventually negotiated for survival. The resulting pact granted them a protected enclave in what is now [[Upper South Booftown]] and acknowledged their right to participate in the new nation’s prosperity.

The settlers later discovered [[Arcannabis]], an extraordinary plant whose magical properties became the foundation of the island’s economy. Properly cultivated, Arcannabis could heighten the senses, expand magical abilities, and reveal visions of unseen realms. [[Arcannabis Cultivation]] became a specialized tradition passed from generation to generation, and merchants soon traveled from distant lands to purchase the crop.

Economic prosperity did not erase the divisions created by colonization. Human settlers and Halfling communities continued to live with distrust, cultural conflict, and unequal access to power. Over time, their traditions and technologies blended into a distinctive culture of music, art, food, and festivals. This cultural exchange created a shared identity, but racial tensions never disappeared entirely.

Stickyickistan’s modern identity is therefore built on both coexistence and unresolved history. Its architecture, markets, and festivals reflect the fusion of Halfling traditions with Human innovation, while the island’s political institutions continue to bear the marks of conquest and resistance.

## The Doobius House Resistance

Stickyickistan was once a nation with several population centers rather than a single city-state. The main [[Human]] settlement on [[Nevercough Island]] was [[Nevercough City]], named for its patriarchal noble family. Across the [[Percolat Inlet]], [[Bongstad]] was carved into the base of [[Mount Zooka]]. The native [[Halfling]] reserve occupied land between a great lava river and the mountain’s slopes, where the terrain was barely habitable.

Farther inland, [[Doobius House]] was founded by [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] as the “Gate to the Outback.” The frontier settlement attracted adventurers, prospectors, artificers, and others willing to live beyond the protection of the coastal communities. At its height, Doobius House rivaled [[Nevercough City]] and became famous for producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines.

Its frontier role gave Doobius House an unusual population. Elyrian settlers, native Halflings, craftspeople, hunters, and exiles lived beside one another, though not as equals. The Highblades claimed the land and profited from its workshops, while the Twothirdlings and other native communities supplied much of the local knowledge, labor, and military experience that kept the settlement alive.

When [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] died, his Human heirs inherited the family’s formal authority and attempted to preserve the old order. The [[Twothirdlings]], who heavily outnumbered the Elyrian population around Doobius House, rejected that arrangement. Led by [[Jimmyjock Labingi]], the duke’s disinherited Twothirdling son, they seized the estate and surrounding settlement. They declared that Doobius House belonged to the people who had made it livable and defended it.

Jimmyjock formed a provisional government and began negotiations with the Elyrian nobility of [[Nevercough City]]. The negotiations quickly failed. The nobles refused to recognize the Twothirdlings’ claim, while Jimmyjock refused to surrender the land or accept an arrangement that would leave his mother’s people subject to the family that had rejected him.

## The [[Arcane Civil War]]

The dispute over Doobius House became one of the first major armed conflicts between Elyrian settlers and the native resistance. House Highblade forces tried to retake the estate and secure the frontier road, while volunteers from Doobius House fortified the settlement and turned the surrounding wilderness into a weapon.

The resulting skirmishes spread into what is now called the [[Grim Forest]]. Doobius House’s militia was badly outnumbered, but its fighters knew the terrain intimately. They attacked at night, cut supply lines, sabotaged war machines, and disappeared into the forest before larger Elyrian forces could respond. Old arcane ballistae, nature-infused war machines, trained beasts, and improvised traps allowed the resistance to ambush troops who expected a quick victory.

The houses disagreed over how quickly the frontier should be conquered, who would control its resources, and whether the Twothirdlings should be expelled, absorbed, or granted limited autonomy. Rival nobles supported, supplied, or undermined the campaign according to their own interests. As the dispute widened, the conflict spread beyond the frontier. Industrial sabotage disrupted foundries and supply depots. Magical duels between noble arcanists devastated sections of the growing settlements. Factions summoned fiends, created unstable war golems, and unleashed necromantic plagues in attempts to gain the upper hand. The original dispute over Doobius House became only one front in a larger struggle for control of the island’s government, resources, and future.

The war was fought through espionage and sabotage as much as open battle. Couriers disappeared along frontier roads, military contracts changed hands through bribery, and entire workshops were destroyed rather than allowed to fall into an enemy’s hands. The [[Grim Forest]] became a maze of abandoned siege engines, burned supply routes, hidden militia camps, and battlefields reclaimed by rapidly growing vegetation.

To the resistance, it proved that settlers could be defeated. To the nobles, it proved that frontier autonomy threatened the authority of every ruling house. The conflict widened into a prolonged civil war that reshaped the island’s political order.

As the cost of the campaign mounted, the nobles of Nevercough City grew weary of trying to dominate a settlement that refused to surrender. Doobius House could not be conquered cheaply, and continued warfare threatened trade routes and the stability of the coastal settlements. The wider civil war also forced the houses to redirect troops and resources away from the frontier.

Jimmyjock used his knowledge of Elyrian law and military practice, combined with the indigenous values of his mother’s people, to negotiate a settlement. The final agreement recognized the Twothirdlings’ right to govern Doobius House while allowing Elyrian families and institutions to remain under negotiated protections. The settlement did not erase the violence or the unequal power that produced it, but it prevented House Highblade from reclaiming the town by force.

Doobius House remained an autonomous and heavily armed frontier community for generations. Its workshops continued producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines, officially to defend against the dangers of [[The Outback]], but also as a reminder that the town’s independence had been won through resistance. Jimmyjock’s songs preserved the memory of the conflict, while Elyrian histories recast him as a rebel and thief of noble property.

After the [[Arcane Civil War]], the surviving settlements eventually united into the city-state of Stickyickistan. Doobius House lost much of its former independence as roads, bureaucracy, and urban expansion absorbed the frontier town into the wider state. Even so, the resistance remains central to its identity. It was the place where the Twothirdlings first proved that Elyrian settlements could be challenged, and where Jimmyjock Labingi turned a disputed inheritance into a homeland.

Long ago, the island’s only humanoid inhabitants were peaceful Halfling communities. They followed a polytheistic faith devoted to [[The Three Sisters]], lived in close relationship with the land, and respected the creatures that shared it. The island flourished, its soil was fertile, and its forests teemed with life.

The settlers established [[Nevercough City]] on what they called [[Nevercough Island]], forming the nation that would eventually become Stickyickistan.

The Halflings resisted, but they were outnumbered and outmatched. Their leaders eventually negotiated for survival. The resulting pact granted them a protected enclave in what is now [[Upper South Booftown]] and acknowledged their right to participate in the new nation’s prosperity.

The settlers later discovered [[Arcannabis]], an extraordinary plant whose magical properties became the foundation of the island’s economy. Properly cultivated, Arcannabis could heighten the senses, expand magical abilities, and reveal visions of unseen realms. [[Arcannabis Cultivation]] became a specialized tradition passed from generation to generation, and merchants soon traveled from distant lands to purchase the crop.

Economic prosperity did not erase the divisions created by colonization. Human settlers and Halfling communities continued to live with distrust, cultural conflict, and unequal access to power. Over time, their traditions and technologies blended into a distinctive culture of music, art, food, and festivals. This cultural exchange created a shared identity, but racial tensions never disappeared entirely.

Stickyickistan’s modern identity is therefore built on both coexistence and unresolved history. Its architecture, markets, and festivals reflect the fusion of Halfling traditions with Human innovation, while the island’s political institutions continue to bear the marks of conquest and resistance.

Farther inland, [[Doobius House]] was founded by [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] as the “Gate to the Outback.” The frontier settlement attracted adventurers, prospectors, artificers, and others willing to live beyond the protection of the coastal communities. At its height, Doobius House rivaled [[Nevercough City]] and became famous for producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines.

Its frontier role gave Doobius House an unusual population. Elyrian settlers, native Halflings, craftspeople, hunters, and exiles lived beside one another, though not as equals. The Highblades claimed the land and profited from its workshops, while the Twothirdlings and other native communities supplied much of the local knowledge, labor, and military experience that kept the settlement alive.

Led by [[Jimmyjock Labingi]], the duke’s disinherited Twothirdling son, they seized the estate and surrounding settlement. They declared that Doobius House belonged to the people who had made it livable and defended it.

Jimmyjock formed a provisional government and began negotiations with the Elyrian nobility of [[Nevercough City]]. The negotiations quickly failed. The nobles refused to recognize the Twothirdlings’ claim, while Jimmyjock refused to surrender the land or accept an arrangement that would leave his mother’s people subject to the family that had rejected him.

The dispute over Doobius House became one of the first major armed conflicts between Elyrian settlers and the native resistance. House Highblade forces tried to retake the estate and secure the frontier road, while volunteers from Doobius House fortified the settlement and turned the surrounding wilderness into a weapon.

They attacked at night, cut supply lines, sabotaged war machines, and disappeared into the forest before larger Elyrian forces could respond. Old arcane ballistae, nature-infused war machines, trained beasts, and improvised traps allowed the resistance to ambush troops who expected a quick victory.

The fighting around Doobius House became entangled with the wider power struggle among the [[Four Founding Houses]]. The houses disagreed over how quickly the frontier should be conquered, who would control its resources, and whether the Twothirdlings should be expelled, absorbed, or granted limited autonomy. Rival nobles supported, supplied, or undermined the campaign according to their own interests. As the dispute widened, the conflict spread beyond the frontier. Industrial sabotage disrupted foundries and supply depots. Magical duels between noble arcanists devastated sections of the growing settlements. Factions summoned fiends, created unstable war golems, and unleashed necromantic plagues in attempts to gain the upper hand. The original dispute over Doobius House became only one front in a larger struggle for control of the island’s government, resources, and future.

The war was fought through espionage and sabotage as much as open battle. Couriers disappeared along frontier roads, military contracts changed hands through bribery, and entire workshops were destroyed rather than allowed to fall into an enemy’s hands. The [[Grim Forest]] became a maze of abandoned siege engines, burned supply routes, hidden militia camps, and battlefields reclaimed by rapidly growing vegetation.

The wider civil war also forced the houses to redirect troops and resources away from the frontier.

The final agreement recognized the Twothirdlings’ right to govern Doobius House while allowing Elyrian families and institutions to remain under negotiated protections. The settlement did not erase the violence or the unequal power that produced it, but it prevented House Highblade from reclaiming the town by force.

Its workshops continued producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines, officially to defend against the dangers of [[The Outback]], but also as a reminder that the town’s independence had been won through resistance. Its origins lie in collapsed bone vaults and necropolis tunnels that opened into deeper Underdark channels, creating a refuge for the poor, the diseased, the dead, and the unwanted.

Beyond the city lies [[The Outback]], a vast expanse of arcane forests, swamps, bogs, mountains, jungles, rainforests, beaches, badlands, and desert. The region is largely unexplored and inhabited by hermits, cults, exiles, rogue druids, forgotten warlocks, and creatures from across the multiverse. The Outback’s raw magic, combined with Mount Zooka’s influence, has made Stickyickistan a hotspot in the multiverse. For bounty hunters, smugglers, prospectors, and treasure seekers, its wilderness promises lost knowledge and untapped power. It also promises that something dangerous is always waiting beyond the city’s last road.

# Past Stickyickistan

Stickyickistan did not always have its current tropical climate. In earlier ages, the island maintained a more balanced pattern of hot and cold regions, as well as arid and humid zones. The northern part once held an ice cap, while the south resembled a Mediterranean climate more than a Caribbean one. Industrialization caused severe climate change. Rising temperatures melted the ice cap and turned some old-growth forests into desert. Recent conservation efforts have slowed the damage, but much of the original landscape has been lost.

Long ago, the island’s humanoid inhabitants were small communities of [[Halflings]], [[Eladrin]], [[Goblins]], and [[Lizardfolk]]. Many followed a polytheistic faith devoted to [[The Three Sisters]], lived in close relationship with the land, and respected the creatures that shared it. The Halflings resisted, but they were outnumbered and outmatched. Their leaders eventually negotiated for survival. The resulting pact granted them a protected enclave in what is now [[Upper South Booftown]] and acknowledged their right to participate in the new nation’s prosperity.

The settlers later discovered [[Arcannabis]], an extraordinary plant whose magical properties became the foundation of the island’s economy. Properly cultivated, Arcannabis could heighten the senses, expand magical abilities, and reveal visions of unseen realms. At its height, Doobius House rivaled [[Nevercough City]] and became famous for producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines.

Led by [[Jimmyjock Labingi]], the duke’s disinherited Twothirdling son, they seized the estate and surrounding settlement. They declared that Doobius House belonged to the people who had made it livable and defended it.

Jimmyjock formed a provisional government and began negotiations with the Elyrian nobility of [[Nevercough City]]. The negotiations quickly failed. The nobles refused to recognize the Twothirdlings’ claim, while Jimmyjock refused to surrender the land or accept an arrangement that would leave his mother’s people subject to the family that had rejected him.

## The [[Arcane Civil War]]

The dispute over Doobius House became one of the first major armed conflicts between Elyrian settlers and the native resistance. House Highblade forces tried to retake the estate and secure the frontier road, while volunteers from Doobius House fortified the settlement and turned the surrounding wilderness into a weapon.

They attacked at night, cut supply lines, sabotaged war machines, and disappeared into the forest before larger Elyrian forces could respond. Old arcane ballistae, nature-infused war machines, trained beasts, and improvised traps allowed the resistance to ambush troops who expected a quick victory.

The fighting around Doobius House became entangled with the wider power struggle among the [[Four Founding Houses]]. The houses disagreed over how quickly the frontier should be conquered, who would control its resources, and whether the Twothirdlings should be expelled, absorbed, or granted limited autonomy. Rival nobles supported, supplied, or undermined the campaign according to their own interests. House Highblade demanded that its claim be restored by force, while other factions used the conflict to weaken Highblade influence and seize the roads, workshops, and military technology produced at Doobius House.

As the dispute widened, the conflict spread beyond the frontier. Industrial sabotage disrupted foundries and supply depots. Magical duels between noble arcanists devastated sections of the growing settlements. Factions summoned fiends, created unstable war golems, and unleashed necromantic plagues in attempts to gain the upper hand. The war was fought through espionage and sabotage as much as open battle. Couriers disappeared along frontier roads, military contracts changed hands through bribery, and entire workshops were destroyed rather than allowed to fall into an enemy’s hands. The [[Grim Forest]] became a maze of abandoned siege engines, burned supply routes, hidden militia camps, and battlefields reclaimed by rapidly growing vegetation.

The Twothirdling resistance did not cause the entire [[Arcane Civil War]], but it exposed the weakness of Elyrian rule. Doobius House became a symbol for both sides. To the resistance, it proved that settlers could be defeated. To the nobles, it proved that frontier autonomy threatened the authority of every ruling house. The conflict widened into a prolonged civil war that reshaped the island’s political order.

Doobius House could not be conquered cheaply, and continued warfare threatened trade routes and the stability of the coastal settlements. The wider civil war also forced the houses to redirect troops and resources away from the frontier.

Jimmyjock used his knowledge of Elyrian law and military practice, combined with the indigenous values of his mother’s people, to negotiate a settlement. The final agreement recognized the Twothirdlings’ right to govern Doobius House while allowing Elyrian families and institutions to remain under negotiated protections. The settlement did not erase the violence or the unequal power that produced it, but it prevented House Highblade from reclaiming the town by force.

Doobius House remained an autonomous and heavily armed frontier community for generations. Its workshops continued producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines, officially to defend against the dangers of [[The Outback]], but also as a reminder that the town’s independence had been won through resistance. Jimmyjock’s songs preserved the memory of the conflict, while Elyrian histories recast him as a rebel and thief of noble property.

After the [[Arcane Civil War]], the surviving settlements eventually united into the city-state of Stickyickistan. Doobius House lost much of its former independence as roads, bureaucracy, and urban expansion absorbed the frontier town into the wider state. Even so, the resistance remains central to its identity. It was the place where the Twothirdlings first proved that Elyrian settlements could be challenged, and where Jimmyjock Labingi turned a disputed inheritance into a homeland.

Few outsiders enter without a contract, and fewer leave without becoming part of someone else’s case file.

South of Nevercough Island and north of the volcano lies [[Lower South Booftown]], commonly called [[Booftown]]. This middle-class district is known for family-owned shops, public parks, and neighborhoods that remain relatively stable despite the city’s larger conflicts. A slow-moving river of thick, dark lava separates it from [[Upper South Booftown]], known as [[The Ashtray]].

The Ashtray is a smoke-blackened district of crooked tenements, ash-slick alleys, rooftop walkways, hidden grow rooms, and half-legal additions built over generations. Its native [[Halfling|halfling]] population is large, but it also shelters outcasts, fugitives, smugglers, mercenaries, failed apprentices, and anyone too useful, desperate, or dangerous to fit elsewhere. The [[Mandem on Booftown]] and [[Cough City Crew]] fight over Arcannabis, underground fighting, protection rackets, gambling, bootlegged [[Alcohol]], and black-market Magitech. Neither gang fully controls the district; power changes from block to block and rooftop to rooftop.

The Ashtray’s residents rely on local networks more than official law. The Sootsteps connect rooftops and exterior stairways, the Cinder Courts host dice games and informal trials, and the Black Stalls sell stolen goods, poisons, counterfeit papers, and illegal Magitech parts. To outsiders, the district is dangerous. To locals, it is home.

To the east of the volcano lies [[Bobo Bush Estates]], where merchant lords, arcane industrialists, politicians, and retired crime bosses live in lavish villas protected by enchanted gardens and high-security Magitech. Deals worth more than a kingdom’s treasury are made over fine Arcannabis and aged Zooka Malt. Espionage, blackmail, and silent assassinations decide more than elections ever do.

North Booftown is the center of food production and Arcannabis cultivation. Its volcanic soil produces crops that grow larger, faster, and stronger than those found elsewhere. The region also belongs to [[House Northbourne]], the least powerful noble house in the [[Nevercough Tribunal]]. Publicly, the Northbournes dominate animal breeding, training, and handling. They own [[The North Booftown Downs]] and founded the [[Handler’s Guild]], whose expertise includes prized racehorses, exotic creatures, and [[Magebred Animals]].

In criminal circles, the Northbournes are called [[The Norfies]]. The family does not use the name, since it can imply criminal affiliations and attract the attention of the [[Nevercough Tribunal]] or the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]]. Behind their respectable public image, the Norfies control much of the city-state’s illicit [[Alcohol]] trade, manipulate racing odds and outcomes, operate gambling syndicates, and host underground fighting rings. Their agents and intermediaries preserve the noble family’s plausible deniability.

The eastern and northern farmlands contain competing estates, guilds, smugglers, and cultivation operations. Farmers in [[Astallon Acres]] benefit from generous wages, while independent growers and criminal producers compete over land, water, and access to the city’s markets. A visitor can cross from a peaceful farmstead into a smuggling route or gang-controlled field without ever seeing a boundary marker.

On the western side of the city, [[Bongstad]] is a Dwarven settlement carved into Mount Zooka. Its maze of tunnels, bridges, terraces, and magitech pipes carries molten slag and processed Arcanite between refineries and forges. Bongstad combines old Dwarven traditions with Arcannabis-fueled invention. Miners and blacksmiths share the settlement with inventors, alchemists, and experimental herbalists. Visitors are advised to bring a strong constitution, a high tolerance for [[Zooka Malt]], and no outstanding gambling debts.

Beneath the city lies [[The Undercity Osslurraggath]], an underground metropolis ignored by the urban elite and denied official recognition by the Nevercough Tribunal. It is home to [[The Mortuary]], the [[Dungsweepers]], exiles, criminals, and people the surface city would rather forget. Its provisional government has little legal authority, but it governs the people who live below. The city began as bone vaults and necropolises before collapsing into deeper Underdark channels, where the [[Heralds of Dust]] established their own philosophy of decay.

Beyond the city lies [[The Outback]], a largely unexplored wilderness where civilization gives way to ancient ruins, arcane forests, hidden rivers, swamps, bogs, mountains, beaches, and anomalies. [[Springwood]] is a massive naturalized park and sacred woodland that remains in an impossible state of spring. Its nearby settlements include [[Kerning’s Crossing]], known for apothecaries and its reliance on the [[Solarium Botanica]]. Recently, seeds and creatures from the Fey realm have begun transforming the forest, creating faerie rings, strange storms, dangerous overgrowth, and new flora such as honeyvine and glowshrooms.

Farther out, [[Doobius House]] remains a run-down frontier village inhabited mainly by indigenous [[Twothirdlings]] and a few full Halflings. Its former importance came from its role as the Gate to the Outback and from the military workshops established there during the resistance against Elyrian expansion. The [[Grim Forest]] borders the village, its history known mainly through indigenous oral traditions. The forest contains hostile plants and undead, while an ancient awakened radiant tree guards its edge.

The Outback also contains [[Zooka Mire]], a swamp just beyond the city limits where the [[Zooka Mire Collective]] operates, and the distant [[Molten Maw]], an underground volcanic city inhabited mainly by [[Duergar]] and [[Svirfneblin]]. Molten Maw’s Veins are semi-intelligent rivers of magical lava, while its Silt Road moves contraband, monster parts, forbidden magic, fugitives, and secrets beneath surface authorities.


The [[Industrial Zone]] is a district devoted almost entirely to manufacturing. It contains no ordinary residences and few public shops. Most of Stickyickistan’s Magitech innovations are developed there, including the operations of [[Tokenheim Extractions Inc.]] and the [[Seekers' Scrapyard]]. Waste from the zone is collected and repurposed by groups such as [[The Seekers of the Vein]], the [[Zooka Mire Collective]], and [[The Iron Sovereign]].

Beneath the city lies [[The Undercity Osslurraggath]], an underground metropolis largely ignored by the elites above. The [[Mortuary]] and the [[Dungsweepers]] operate there, alongside undesirables, exiles, and communities that the surface government refuses to acknowledge. Osslurraggath has a provisional government, but the [[Nevercough Tribunal]] recognizes no authority beneath the city. Its origins lie in collapsed bone vaults and necropolis tunnels that opened into deeper Underdark channels, creating a refuge for the poor, the diseased, the dead, and the unwanted.

Beyond the city lies [[The Outback]], a vast expanse of arcane forests, swamps, bogs, mountains, jungles, rainforests, beaches, badlands, and desert. The region is largely unexplored and inhabited by hermits, cults, exiles, rogue druids, forgotten warlocks, and creatures from across the multiverse. The [[Zooka Mire]] is a swamp just beyond the city limits where the [[Zooka Mire Collective]] operates. Farther afield, [[Springwood]] is an ancient sacred woodland and naturalized park where Fey influence has begun to alter the seasons, landscape, flora, and fauna. [[Doobius House]] lies deeper in The Outback, while the [[Grim Forest]] marks a dangerous region of hostile plants, undead, and old battlefields.

The Outback’s raw magic, combined with Mount Zooka’s influence, has made Stickyickistan a hotspot in the multiverse. For bounty hunters, smugglers, prospectors, and treasure seekers, its wilderness promises lost knowledge and untapped power. It also promises that something dangerous is always waiting beyond the city’s last road.

# Past Stickyickistan

Stickyickistan did not always have its current tropical climate. In earlier ages, the island maintained a more balanced pattern of hot and cold regions, as well as arid and humid zones. The northern part once held an ice cap, while the south resembled a Mediterranean climate more than a Caribbean one. Industrialization caused severe climate change. Rising temperatures melted the ice cap and turned some old-growth forests into desert. Recent conservation efforts have slowed the damage, but much of the original landscape has been lost.

## [[Human Colonialism]]

Long ago, the island’s humanoid inhabitants were small communities of [[Halflings]], [[Eladrin]], [[Goblins]], and [[Lizardfolk]]. Many followed a polytheistic faith devoted to [[The Three Sisters]], lived in close relationship with the land, and respected the creatures that shared it. The island flourished, its soil was fertile, and its forests teemed with life.

That balance was disrupted when ambitious Human settlers arrived. Seeking control of the island’s resources, they treated the Halflings as obstacles and launched a violent invasion. The settlers established [[Nevercough City]] on what they called [[Nevercough Island]], forming the nation that would eventually become Stickyickistan.

The Halflings resisted, but they were outnumbered and outmatched. Their leaders eventually negotiated for survival. The resulting pact granted them a protected enclave in what is now [[Upper South Booftown]] and acknowledged their right to participate in the new nation’s prosperity.

The settlers later discovered [[Arcannabis]], an extraordinary plant whose magical properties became the foundation of the island’s economy. Properly cultivated, Arcannabis could heighten the senses, expand magical abilities, and reveal visions of unseen realms. [[Arcannabis Cultivation]] became a specialized tradition passed from generation to generation, and merchants soon traveled from distant lands to purchase the crop.

Economic prosperity did not erase the divisions created by colonization. Human settlers and Halfling communities continued to live with distrust, cultural conflict, and unequal access to power. Over time, their traditions and technologies blended into a distinctive culture of music, art, food, and festivals. This cultural exchange created a shared identity, but racial tensions never disappeared entirely.

Stickyickistan’s modern identity is therefore built on both coexistence and unresolved history. Its architecture, markets, and festivals reflect the fusion of Halfling traditions with Human innovation, while the island’s political institutions continue to bear the marks of conquest and resistance.

## The Doobius House Resistance

Stickyickistan was once a nation with several population centers rather than a single city-state. The main [[Human]] settlement on [[Nevercough Island]] was [[Nevercough City]], named for its patriarchal noble family. Across the [[Percolat Inlet]], [[Bongstad]] was carved into the base of [[Mount Zooka]]. The native [[Halfling]] reserve occupied land between a great lava river and the mountain’s slopes, where the terrain was barely habitable.

Farther inland, [[Doobius House]] was founded by [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] as the “Gate to the Outback.” The frontier settlement attracted adventurers, prospectors, artificers, and others willing to live beyond the protection of the coastal communities. At its height, Doobius House rivaled [[Nevercough City]] and became famous for producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines.

Its frontier role gave Doobius House an unusual population. Elyrian settlers, native Halflings, craftspeople, hunters, and exiles lived beside one another, though not as equals. The Highblades claimed the land and profited from its workshops, while the Twothirdlings and other native communities supplied much of the local knowledge, labor, and military experience that kept the settlement alive.

When [[Duke Doobius Highblade]] died, his Human heirs inherited the family’s formal authority and attempted to preserve the old order. The [[Twothirdlings]], who heavily outnumbered the Elyrian population around Doobius House, rejected that arrangement. Led by [[Jimmyjock Labingi]], the duke’s disinherited Twothirdling son, they seized the estate and surrounding settlement. They declared that Doobius House belonged to the people who had made it livable and defended it.

Jimmyjock formed a provisional government and began negotiations with the Elyrian nobility of [[Nevercough City]]. The negotiations quickly failed. The nobles refused to recognize the Twothirdlings’ claim, while Jimmyjock refused to surrender the land or accept an arrangement that would leave his mother’s people subject to the family that had rejected him.

## The [[Arcane Civil War]]

The dispute over Doobius House became one of the first major armed conflicts between Elyrian settlers and the native resistance. House Highblade forces tried to retake the estate and secure the frontier road, while volunteers from Doobius House fortified the settlement and turned the surrounding wilderness into a weapon.

The resulting skirmishes spread into what is now called the [[Grim Forest]]. Doobius House’s militia was badly outnumbered, but its fighters knew the terrain intimately. They attacked at night, cut supply lines, sabotaged war machines, and disappeared into the forest before larger Elyrian forces could respond. Old arcane ballistae, nature-infused war machines, trained beasts, and improvised traps allowed the resistance to ambush troops who expected a quick victory.

The fighting around Doobius House became entangled with the wider power struggle among the [[Four Founding Houses]]. The houses disagreed over how quickly the frontier should be conquered, who would control its resources, and whether the Twothirdlings should be expelled, absorbed, or granted limited autonomy. Rival nobles supported, supplied, or undermined the campaign according to their own interests. House Highblade demanded that its claim be restored by force, while other factions used the conflict to weaken Highblade influence and seize the roads, workshops, and military technology produced at Doobius House.

As the dispute widened, the conflict spread beyond the frontier. Industrial sabotage disrupted foundries and supply depots. Magical duels between noble arcanists devastated sections of the growing settlements. Factions summoned fiends, created unstable war golems, and unleashed necromantic plagues in attempts to gain the upper hand. The original dispute over Doobius House became only one front in a larger struggle for control of the island’s government, resources, and future.

The war was fought through espionage and sabotage as much as open battle. Couriers disappeared along frontier roads, military contracts changed hands through bribery, and entire workshops were destroyed rather than allowed to fall into an enemy’s hands. The [[Grim Forest]] became a maze of abandoned siege engines, burned supply routes, hidden militia camps, and battlefields reclaimed by rapidly growing vegetation.

The Twothirdling resistance did not cause the entire [[Arcane Civil War]], but it exposed the weakness of Elyrian rule. Doobius House became a symbol for both sides. To the resistance, it proved that settlers could be defeated. To the nobles, it proved that frontier autonomy threatened the authority of every ruling house. The conflict widened into a prolonged civil war that reshaped the island’s political order.

As the cost of the campaign mounted, the nobles of Nevercough City grew weary of trying to dominate a settlement that refused to surrender. Doobius House could not be conquered cheaply, and continued warfare threatened trade routes and the stability of the coastal settlements. The wider civil war also forced the houses to redirect troops and resources away from the frontier.

Jimmyjock used his knowledge of Elyrian law and military practice, combined with the indigenous values of his mother’s people, to negotiate a settlement. The final agreement recognized the Twothirdlings’ right to govern Doobius House while allowing Elyrian families and institutions to remain under negotiated protections. The settlement did not erase the violence or the unequal power that produced it, but it prevented House Highblade from reclaiming the town by force.

Doobius House remained an autonomous and heavily armed frontier community for generations. Its workshops continued producing arcane ballistae and nature-infused war machines, officially to defend against the dangers of [[The Outback]], but also as a reminder that the town’s independence had been won through resistance. Jimmyjock’s songs preserved the memory of the conflict, while Elyrian histories recast him as a rebel and thief of noble property.

After the [[Arcane Civil War]], the surviving settlements eventually united into the city-state of Stickyickistan. Doobius House lost much of its former independence as roads, bureaucracy, and urban expansion absorbed the frontier town into the wider state. Even so, the resistance remains central to its identity. It was the place where the Twothirdlings first proved that Elyrian settlements could be challenged, and where Jimmyjock Labingi turned a disputed inheritance into a homeland.

title: History of Stickyickistan
---

The island’s size and distance from other landmasses are difficult to measure. Even the most sophisticated magic and technology fails beyond a certain distance from its shores.

The waters around Stickyickistan form a region much like a magical Bermuda Triangle. Pilots and sailors report violent weather, distorted horizons, impossible currents, and terrifying creatures from above and below. Vast deposits of [[Arcanite]] beneath [[Mount Zooka]] have warped time, space, and the Weave around the island, producing these phenomena and making accurate maps difficult to create. Stickyickistan can be seen from [[Lumytholarispace]] and appears on maps of Mythmos, but it always looks smaller than it seems when approached.

The island’s soil is rich in nutrients and infused with Arcanite. Flora and fauna grow with unusual fertility and magical potency, especially in [[North Booftown]], the agricultural heartland. title: History of Stickyickistan
---

Stickyickistan is an island on the planet of [[Mythmos]], shrouded in magic and home to one of the largest economies in the realms. Its wealth is built primarily on the cultivation and export of [[Arcannabis]], along with trade in [[Arcanite]] and other resources. The island’s size and distance from other landmasses are difficult to measure. Even the most sophisticated magic and technology fails beyond a certain distance from its shores.

The waters around Stickyickistan form a region much like a magical Bermuda Triangle. Pilots and sailors report violent weather, distorted horizons, impossible currents, and terrifying creatures from above and below. Vast deposits of [[Arcanite]] beneath [[Mount Zooka]] have warped time, space, and the Weave around the island, producing these phenomena and making accurate maps difficult to create. Stickyickistan can be seen from [[Lumytholarispace]] and appears on maps of Mythmos, but it always looks smaller than it seems when approached.

![[Stickyickistan.jpg]]

# Modern Stickyickistan

Stickyickistan is a city-state built around the active [[Mount Zooka]], whose obsidian slopes and glowing Arcanite veins dominate the island’s skyline. Approximately 27 million people live across a dense network of terraced districts connected by bridges, roads, canals, lifts, and industrial transit lines. The Capitol stands on [[Nevercough Island]], a small landmass sheltered within the [[Percolat Inlet]]. The climate is generally tropical, with hot, humid weather across the urban core. Farther inland, desertification has created increasingly arid regions, a legacy of [[Human Colonialism]] and industrialization.

The city rises in layers around the volcano. Wealthy residences climb into the jungle, where enchanted gardens and fortified estates overlook the ocean. Beneath them, poorer settlements cling to the mountainside in a haze of ash, smoke, brimstone, and sulfur. Above these districts, the [[Industrial Zone]] follows the crater’s rim and extends into the mountain through mines, foundries, refineries, and [[Magitech]] workshops.

[[Mount Zooka]] is an active [[Arcanite]] Cone, a rare volcano formed above rich deposits of raw Arcanite. Its slopes are black and glassy, marked by glowing veins of molten rock and slow-moving lava flows. Violent eruptions scatter volcanic stone, magma, and chunks of raw Arcanite across the island. Miners, magitech engineers, alchemists, and bounty hunters maintain dangerous outposts along the crater’s rim, searching for ore, magical artifacts, and volatile energy. The Dwarves of [[Bongstad]] have carved a fortified settlement into the mountain’s base, using its heat to power their forges.

Arcanite fuels much of Stickyickistan’s wealth and technology. Once extracted and purified, it can be worked into weapons, armor, artifacts, and industrial systems. The [[Nevercough Tribunal]] and [[The Seekers of the Vein]] operate mines and outposts around the crater, while [[Tokenheim Extractions Inc.]] and other industrial concerns process the ore and produce much of the city-state’s Magitech. Waste from the [[Industrial Zone]] feeds salvage operations at [[Seekers' Scrapyard]] and is collected by groups such as [[The Seekers of the Vein]], [[Zooka Mire Collective]], and [[The Iron Sovereign]].

The island’s soil is rich in nutrients and infused with Arcanite. Flora and fauna grow with unusual fertility and magical potency, especially in [[North Booftown]], the agricultural heartland. [[Astallon Acres]] lies along the wetlands bordering the [[Zooka Mire]], where [[Ezra Astallon]] pays farm workers unusually well and resolves local problems with money. [[Arcannabis]] remains the city-state’s primary export, while Arcanite, magebred animals, and other natural resources provide additional wealth.

Since the arrival of Human colonists, [[Alcohol]] has been outlawed because the government considers it a threat to the Arcannabis market. [[Zooka Malt]], a beverage made from Arcannabis buds, has become the principal alternative to traditional ale. The city’s merchants sell countless infused varieties, from cheap street brews to carefully aged drinks served in the private lounges of [[Bobo Bush Estates]].

[[Nevercough Island]] is the seat of political power and old money. At its heart stands the [[Capitol Building]], where Chief Magistrate [[Dabnar Nevercough]] rules through courts that dispense justice and corruption in equal measure. The island also contains the [[Grand Arcanum Library]], the [[Nevercough Museum]], elite magical academies such as [[N.E.R.D]], high-end boutiques, apothecaries, and specialty Magitech shops. The former settlement of [[Nevercough City]] remains the name commonly used for the island and its historic urban core.

The [[Ashen Citadel]] rises over Nevercough Island as the headquarters of the [[Ashen Shadow Society]], Stickyickistan’s most infamous bounty-hunting guild. Its dark stone walls, Magitech barriers, arcane wards, training facilities, forges, laboratories, archives, and holding cells make it both fortress and command center. Few outsiders enter without a contract, and fewer leave without becoming part of someone else’s case file.

South of Nevercough Island and north of the volcano lies [[Lower South Booftown]], commonly called [[Booftown]]. This middle-class district is known for family-owned shops, public parks, and relatively stable neighborhoods. A slow-moving river of thick, dark lava separates it from [[Upper South Booftown]], known as [[The Ashtray]].

The Ashtray is a smoke-blackened district of crooked tenements, ash-slick alleys, rooftop walkways, hidden grow rooms, and half-legal additions built over generations. Its native [[Halfling|halfling]] population is large, but it also shelters outcasts, fugitives, smugglers, mercenaries, failed apprentices, and anyone too useful, desperate, or dangerous to fit elsewhere. The [[Mandem on Booftown]] and [[Cough City Crew]] fight over Arcannabis, underground fighting, protection rackets, gambling, bootlegged Alcohol, and black-market Magitech. Neither gang fully controls the district. The Sootsteps connect rooftops and exterior stairways, the Cinder Courts host dice games and informal trials, and [[The Black Stalls]] sell stolen goods, poisons, counterfeit papers, and illegal Magitech parts. To outsiders, the district is dangerous. To locals, it is home.

To the east of the volcano lies [[Bobo Bush Estates]], where merchant lords, arcane industrialists, politicians, and retired crime bosses live in lavish villas protected by enchanted gardens and high-security Magitech. Deals worth more than a kingdom’s treasury are made over fine Arcannabis and aged Zooka Malt. Espionage, blackmail, and silent assassinations decide more than elections ever do.

North Booftown is the center of food production and Arcannabis cultivation. Its volcanic soil produces crops that grow larger, faster, and stronger than those found elsewhere. The region also belongs to [[House Northbourne]], the least powerful noble house in the [[Nevercough Tribunal]]. Publicly, the Northbournes dominate animal breeding, training, and handling. They own [[The North Booftown Downs]] and founded the [[Handler’s Guild]], whose expertise includes prized racehorses, exotic creatures, and [[Magebred Animals]].

In criminal circles, the Northbournes are called [[The Norfies]]. The family does not use the name, since it can imply criminal affiliations and attract the attention of the [[Nevercough Tribunal]] or the [[Tribunal Highblade Coalition]]. Behind their respectable public image, the Norfies control much of the city-state’s illicit Alcohol trade, manipulate racing odds and outcomes, operate gambling syndicates, and host underground fighting rings. Their agents and intermediaries preserve the noble family’s plausible deniability.

On the western side of the city, [[Bongstad]] is a Dwarven settlement carved into Mount Zooka. Its maze of tunnels, bridges, terraces, and magitech pipes carries molten slag and processed Arcanite between refineries and forges. Bongstad combines old Dwarven traditions with Arcannabis-fueled invention. Miners and blacksmiths share the settlement with inventors, alchemists, and experimental herbalists. Visitors are advised to bring a strong constitution, a high tolerance for Zooka Malt, and no outstanding gambling debts.

Beneath the city lies [[The Undercity Osslurraggath]], an underground metropolis ignored by the urban elite and denied official recognition by the Nevercough Tribunal. It is home to [[The Mortuary]], the [[Dungsweepers]], exiles, criminals, and people the surface city would rather forget. Its provisional government has little legal authority, but it governs the people who live below. Osslurraggath began as bone vaults and necropolis tunnels before collapsing into deeper Underdark channels, creating a refuge for the poor, the diseased, the dead, and the unwanted. The [[Heralds of Dust]] established a philosophy of decay there.

Beyond the city lies [[The Outback]], a largely unexplored wilderness where civilization gives way to ancient ruins, arcane forests, hidden rivers, swamps, bogs, mountains, beaches, and magical anomalies. [[Springwood]] is a massive naturalized park and sacred woodland that remains in an impossible state of spring. Its settlements include [[Kerning’s Crossing]], known for apothecaries and its reliance on the [[Solarium Botanica]]. Fey influence has begun to alter the forest’s seasons, landscape, flora, and fauna, creating strange storms, faerie rings, dangerous overgrowth, honeyvine, and glowshrooms.

Farther out, [[Doobius House]] remains a humble frontier village inhabited mainly by indigenous [[Twothirdlings]] and a few full Halflings. Its former importance came from its role as the Gate to the Outback and from the military workshops established there during Elyrian expansion. The [[Grim Forest]] borders the village, its history preserved mainly through indigenous oral traditions. The forest contains hostile plants and undead, while an ancient awakened radiant tree guards its edge.

The Outback also contains [[Zooka Mire]], a swamp just beyond the city limits where the [[Zooka Mire Collective]] operates, and the distant [[Molten Maw]], an underground volcanic city inhabited mainly by [[Duergar]] and [[Svirfneblin]]. Molten Maw’s Veins are semi-intelligent rivers of magical lava, while [[The Silt Road]] moves contraband, monster parts, forbidden magic, fugitives, and secrets beneath surface authorities. The Outback’s raw magic, combined with Mount Zooka’s influence, has made Stickyickistan a hotspot in the multiverse. For bounty hunters, smugglers, prospectors, and treasure seekers, its wilderness promises lost knowledge and untapped power. It also promises that something dangerous is always waiting beyond the city’s last road.

# Past Stickyickistan

Stickyickistan did not always have its current tropical climate. In earlier ages, the island maintained a more balanced pattern of hot and cold regions, as well as arid and humid zones. The northern part once held an ice cap, while the south resembled a Mediterranean climate more than a Caribbean one. Industrialization caused severe climate change. Rising temperatures melted the ice cap and turned some old-growth forests into desert. Recent conservation efforts have slowed the damage, but much of the original landscape has been lost.

## [[Human Colonialism]]

Long ago, the island’s humanoid inhabitants were small communities of [[Halflings]], [[Eladrin]], [[Goblins]], and [[Lizardfolk]]. Many followed a polytheistic faith devoted to [[The Three Sisters]], lived in close relationship with the land, and respected the creatures that shared it. The island flourished, its soil was fertile, and its forests teemed with life.

That balance was disrupted when ambitious Human settlers arrived. Seeking control of the island’s resources, they treated the Halflings as obstacles and launched a violent invasion. The settlers established [[Nevercough City]] on what they called [[Nevercough Island]], forming the nation that would eventually become Stickyickistan.

The Halflings resisted, but they were outnumbered and outmatched. Their leaders eventually negotiated for survival. The resulting pact granted them a protected enclave in what is now [[Upper South Booftown]] and acknowledged their right to participate in the new nation’s prosperity.

The settlers later discovered [[Arcannabis]], an extraordinary plant whose magical properties became the foundation of the island’s economy. Properly cultivated, Arcannabis could heighten the senses, expand magical abilities, and reveal visions of unseen realms. [[Arcannabis Cultivation]] became a specialized tradition passed from generation to generation, and merchants soon traveled from distant lands to purchase the crop.

Economic prosperity did not erase the divisions created by colonization. Human settlers and Halfling communities continued to live with distrust, cultural conflict, and unequal access to power. Over time, their traditions and technologies blended into a distinctive culture of music, art, food, and festivals. This cultural exchange created a shared identity, but racial tensions never disappeared entirely.

Stickyickistan’s modern identity is therefore built on both coexistence and unresolved history. Its architecture, markets, and festivals reflect the fusion of Halfling traditions with Human innovation, while the island’s political institutions continue to bear the marks of conquest and resistance.

# Seekers' Scrapyard

The [[Seekers' Scrapyard]] is an 800-acre waste field on the edge of Stickyickistan’s [[Industrial Zone]]. It is owned and operated by [[The Seekers of the Vein]], the mining and jeweler’s guild controlled by [[House Stonemug]]. Every day, the guild sends obsolete equipment, broken extraction machinery, failed [[Magitech]], spent Arcanite casings, slag, damaged tools, and contaminated industrial refuse here rather than paying to transport it farther from the city.

From a distance, the scrapyard looks like a wasteland of rusted gantries, collapsed cranes, slag hills, cracked ore carts, and heaps of blackened metal. Up close, it is an active salvage site. Guild crews sort valuable Arcanite fragments, adamantine scraps, rare gemstones, and reusable components from the waste. Independent scavengers, hired prospectors, and members of [[The Seekers of the Vein]] compete to find anything that can be repaired, refined, or sold. The scrapyard’s proximity to [[Bongstad]] and the city’s Magitech industry makes even its refuse valuable.

The largest sections of the yard are divided into unofficial zones: the slag fields, where molten waste has cooled into jagged black ridges; the machine graveyard, where broken extraction rigs and abandoned Magitech constructs are stored; the chemical ponds, where alchemical runoff collects in brightly colored pools; and the deep heaps, where older waste has been buried beneath newer deposits. Maps of these zones are unreliable because machinery is constantly moved, scavengers dig new routes, and sections of the ground collapse without warning.

The Seekers maintain a guarded salvage depot and a network of temporary watch posts throughout the yard. Their official policy is that all discarded material remains guild property, and scavengers caught stealing valuable components can face fines, imprisonment, or quiet retaliation. In practice, the guild lacks enough personnel to monitor the entire 800 acres. Bribery, forged salvage permits, and territorial agreements with local gangs are common.

The scrapyard’s waste is also collected by groups that use it for their own purposes. [[The Seekers of the Vein]] recover raw materials for mining and jewelry production, while the [[Zooka Mire Collective]] diverts chemical runoff and organic waste toward experiments in the nearby mire. [[The Iron Sovereign]] searches the heaps for discarded Magitech, damaged constructs, and components useful for its warforged revolutionaries. The guild officially condemns these activities, but rarely investigates too closely when the waste disappears without creating a public problem.

## The Cult of Goob’lath

The scrapyard has become a center of activity for the [[Cult of Goob'lath]], a growing sect devoted to [[Goob'lath]], the black slime dragon. Most of the cult’s followers are black-winged kobolds, but oozes and a small number of Humans also venerate the dragon. Cultists hide among scavenger crews, coat themselves in the tar spreading through the deeper sections of the yard, and imitate Goob’lath’s scales as a sign of devotion.

The tar is more than decoration. It allows the cult’s Tar Elementals and other ooze servants to move through parts of the scrapyard with surprising speed. Pools of the substance have appeared near drainage channels, collapsed storage pits, and abandoned processing stations. Some workers believe the tar is industrial waste. Others suspect it is being deliberately spread by the cult as part of a larger ritual.

Cult activity has increased around a sealed section of the yard where the ground is warm, the waste shifts without explanation, and black slime appears even after the area has been cleaned. The Seekers have placed warning signs and guard posts around the site, but they have not admitted publicly that several workers and scavengers have disappeared there.

## The Ruined Alchemical Dungeon

Beneath one of the older waste mounds lies the remains of a ruined alchemical dungeon. The complex was exposed when a collapsed processing platform opened a shaft into the earth. Its original builders are unknown, but the surviving chambers contain cracked glasswork, corroded brass pipes, sealed laboratories, and fragments of alchemical equipment unlike anything currently used in the city.

The dungeon was occupied by black kobolds who attacked the [[Frockfit Builder Clan]], a goblin construction crew hired by the Seekers to build a secure vault inside the ruins. The kobolds had turned parts of the dungeon into a defensible warren and used the surrounding waste heaps as cover for raids. Their attacks stopped after [[Unit BH-Umbra Δ9]], a Bloodhound squad of the [[Ashen Shadow Society]], entered the scrapyard and cleared the site.

During the operation, Unit BH-Umbra Δ9 also defeated a [[Dodecahedrooze]] found within the ruined complex. The creature’s presence suggests that the dungeon’s alchemical remains are still active, contaminated, or capable of producing new life. Several chambers remain sealed, and the goblin builders have been instructed not to open them without written authorization from the Seekers.

The [[Frockfit Builder Clan]] is constructing a fortified vault in the surviving central chambers. Officially, the vault will store rare Arcanite, recovered artifacts, and hazardous industrial materials. Unofficially, the Seekers may also intend to use it to conceal evidence of illegal dumping, experimental waste, cult activity, and any discoveries they do not want the [[Nevercough Tribunal]] to inspect.

## Dangers

Visitors to the scrapyard face more than unstable piles of metal. Common hazards include:

- Collapsing waste heaps and unstable scaffolds.
- Toxic fumes and alchemical runoff.
- Buried Magitech that activates without warning.
- Tar Elementals and other oozes moving through drainage channels.
- Territorial scavengers and armed salvage crews.
- Cultists of Goob’lath disguised as laborers.
- Unstable constructs assembled from discarded parts.
- Hidden shafts leading into the ruined alchemical dungeon.
- Sealed chambers containing forgotten experiments.

## Adventure Hooks

- The Seekers hire the party to recover a valuable Arcanite core from a collapsed machine graveyard.
- A scavenger disappears after finding a sealed entrance beneath the deep heaps.
- The Cult of Goob’lath begins spreading tar toward the Industrial Zone.
- The Frockfit Builder Clan requests protection while opening a new section of the alchemical dungeon.
- A damaged Magitech construct from [[Tokenheim Extractions Inc.]] awakens and begins assembling other machines.
- Unit BH-Umbra Δ9 asks the party to investigate a sealed chamber they were unable to enter.
- The Nevercough Tribunal suspects the Seekers are hiding hazardous waste and sends inspectors into the yard.
- A Dodecahedrooze survives beneath the scrapyard and begins feeding on discarded magical equipment.
